gig.title: Upside Down London
gig.pageText: Pinhole London is building a new pop-up camera obscura at Alexandra Palace this Summer, coinciding with 200 years of the first photograph. Step inside an immersive camera obscura experience this summer and watch London’s wonderful panorama, the park, and the people outside appear before you — live, and upside down. Capture it on your phone and leave with your own piece of photographic history. Supported by Arts Council England. Follow Pinhole London on Instagram and Eventbrite for updates.

gig.title: Royal Philharmonic Orchestra and Mandle Cheung
gig.pageText: Live at Alexandra Palace Theatre this August, Mandle Cheung leads the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra and the Brighton Festival Chorus, joined by soloists Elizabeth Watts and Jennifer Johnston. From the searching intensity of its opening movement to the hushed entrance of the chorus and the radiant affirmation of its closing pages, Gustav Mahler’s Second Symphony unfolds as a deeply human journey. One of the composer’s most expansive works, the “Resurrection Symphony” confronts questions of loss, faith, and renewal on a monumental scale. Suitable for all ages. Key information About Mandle Cheung In 2017, Cheung founded the Mandle Philharmonic Orchestra in Toronto, Canada. Since then, the ensemble has presented 19 concert programmes to largely sold-out audiences at leading venues across the city, performing repertoire including Beethoven’s Symphony No. 9, ‘Choral’ and various symphonies by Brahms, Tchaikovsky, and Mahler. In June 2025, Cheung conducted the Toronto Symphony Orchestra in a performance of Mahler’s Symphony No. 2, further demonstrating his affinity for the composer’s music.

gig.title: Norman Jay MBE presents Good Times
gig.pageText: A note from Norman Jay MBE: It is with genuine sadness and deep regret to inform everyone that Good Times at Alexandra Palace will no longer be going ahead this year. Due to unforeseen circumstances beyond our control, including my personal ongoing health challenges, I have had to make the incredibly difficult decision to step away from hosting this year’s event. This wasn’t a decision taken lightly, and I am deeply sorry for everyone who was looking forward to celebrating with us. I want to reassure you that this decision relates only to Good Times at Alexandra Palace. I’ll still be performing at festivals and events throughout the summer, and I can’t wait to see many of you out on the road. All ticket holders will be automatically refunded to the card used to purchase their tickets. Please allow 3–10 working days for the refund to appear in your account, depending on your card provider. Thank you for all your continued love, support and understanding; it truly means the world to me. Good Times has always been about the community we’ve built together, and I’m grateful to every one of you for being part of it. With much love and maximum respect, Norman Jay MBE

gig.title: London Squash Classic
gig.pageText: The London Squash Classic is back at Alexandra Palace Theatre following its spectacular debut last year, with the 2026 edition set to take place between 2 – 6 September, once again featuring both a men’s and women’s draw. The Gold-level event became an instant favourite amongst squash fans new and old last year, with the gladiatorial battles thrilling capacity crowds in the bear-pit atmosphere of the amphitheatre. For the past 2 years we saw the world’s best squash players descend on Alexandra Palace, with Egypt’s Amina Orfi capturing the women’s title, while New Zealand’s former World No.1 Paul Coll put in a series of spectacular performances to secure the men’s title. The world’s best will be back again this September, join us for an amazing spectacle of squash!

gig.title: Annie Mac
gig.pageText: Dance at Annie Mac‘s much‑loved Before Midnight at Ally Pally this September. Expect an inclusive, high‑energy dancefloor with one simple rule: no phones, just vibes. Come early, dance freely, and be home before midnight. A DJ, broadcaster and author with a 20‑year legacy in music and culture, Annie Mac is known for curating joyful, meaningful club experiences. Since launching in 2022, Before Midnight has become a sell‑out phenomenon, celebrated for its welcoming atmosphere and irresistible energy. Join us for feel‑good clubbing from one of the most authentic voices in music! Age restriction 18+

gig.title: ANOTR
gig.pageText: ANOTR bring their biggest UK headline show to date to Alexandra Palace’s Great Hall this September. New date added due to phenomenal demand, 17 September 2026 Making their debut at the beloved North London venue, the Amsterdam duo arrive at a defining moment with their third album, Withness, a dancefloor-focused project shaped across clubs and festivals worldwide. Following the success of Talk To You, ANOTR’s groove-led, soulful sound reaches new heights. Age restriction 18+

gig.title: Monteverdi Choir – Rossini’s Petite Messe Solennelle
gig.pageText: Join us this autumn at Alexandra Palace Theatre as the Monteverdi Choir & Orchestras continue their groundbreaking exploration of Rossini on period instruments, culminating in the crowning achievement of the composer’s final creative years: the Petite messe solennelle. The Monteverdi Choir’s versatility from 17th-century sacred music to 19th-century opera make it the ideal vehicle for this choral showpiece, while the Orchestre Révolutionnaire et Romantique will draw on its deep experience of French Romantic repertoire to recreate the sound world of Rossini’s Paris. Together, with a cast of exceptional soloists and led by Rossini specialist Jakob Lehmann, they will illuminate a work poised between devotion and drama, liturgy and theatre. Age recommendation: all ages

gig.title: Palace Performing Arts
gig.pageText: A performing arts programme for young people aged 7–18 at Alexandra Palace, with classes for Little Stars (7–10 years), Shooting Stars (11–14 years) and Supernovas (15–18 years). From first-time performers to those with experience on stage, Palace Performing Arts gives young people the opportunity to sing, dance and act while developing their creativity, building confidence and making new friendships. Led by experienced industry professionals, our Saturday sessions encourage every young person to express themselves, discover new skills and enjoy performing in a welcoming and supportive environment. Throughout the year, every young person works towards exciting opportunities to perform, including on the iconic Alexandra Palace Theatre stage. If you wish to sign up once the term has started, or need support with payment please speak to a member of the team to discuss payment plan options via visitor.services@alexandrapalace.com or by calling 020 8365 4343. KEY INFORMATION AUTUMN TERM DATES Sat 19 Sept Sat 26 Sept Sat 3 Oct Sat 10 Oct Sat 17 Oct Sat 24 Oct Sat 14 Nov Sat 21 Nov Sat 28 Nov Sat 5 Dec WHAT'S THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN LITTLE STARS, SHOOTING STARS & SUPERNOVAS? Little Stars (7–10 year-olds): A fun introduction to singing, dancing and acting, where young performers build confidence, make friends and discover the joy of performing as they prepare for their first performance in the Alexandra Palace Theatre. Shooting Stars (11-14 year-olds): Building creativity and stage skills through singing, dancing and acting, while taking on new challenges, working together and gaining experience performing on the Alexandra Palace Theatre stage. Supernovas (15 – 18 year-olds): Taking performance to the next level through singing, acting and dance, and refining stagecraft and artistic expression ahead of productions in the Alexandra Palace Theatre.

gig.title: Boris Brejcha
gig.pageText: Boris Brejcha makes his debut at Alexandra Palace this September for his biggest ever UK show as part of his 2026 Reflections Tour. The king of high-tech minimal and man in the mask will unveil an immersive stage production designed exclusively for the space, turning our Great Hall into a surreal theatre of movement and precision-engineered visuals. Renowned for his Joker mask and pioneering sound, Brejcha has captivated global audiences for over two decades, with standout performances at Tomorrowland and for Cercle, which have amassed over 160 million views. Age restriction 18+

gig.title: Illustrating Children’s Books Course for Adults
gig.pageText: Have you ever had a story you’ve always dreamed of turning into a children’s book? Join us for a 10-week course every Wednesday morning in our Creativity Pavilion. During the course, we will explore the world of illustrations for children’s books, looking into every step of the artistic and narrative process to create picture books. For more info and details about this course, please email judi.ga@gmail.com Please note: if the minimum number of students is not reached, the course will not be able to go ahead and refunds will be provided.

gig.title: I Prevail
gig.pageText: GRAMMY-nominated metalcore heavyweights I Prevail will storm the Palace in September 2026. Formed in Metro Detroit, Michigan in 2013, I Prevail have risen to become one of modern metalcore’s most dynamic forces. Following the success of Lifelines (2016), TRAUMA (2019), and TRUE POWER (2022), the band now enter a bold new chapter with their fourth album Violent Nature. Self-produced at Nashville’s Blackbird Studios under the guidance of bassist/keyboardist Jon Eberhard, the record marks vocalist Eric Vanlerberghe’s debut as the group’s sole singer, delivering both clean and unclean vocals with ferocious intensity. From the brutal title track to the soaring anthem Rain, Violent Nature captures the extremes of I Prevail’s sound, balancing aggression and vulnerability in equal measure. Welcome, then, to the new era of I Prevail. Not only is this the best version of the band to date, but it bristles with intention, passion and energy. With support from Amira Elfeky, Polaris and Gore. Age restriction 16+

gig.title: Friday Night is Music Night with Joe Stilgoe
gig.pageText: Jazz sensation and entertainer extraordinaire, Joe Stilgoe joins Fiona Monbet and the BBC Concert Orchestra at Alexandra Palace Theatre for an all-swinging, all-singing edition of Friday Night is Music Night. Singer, pianist, bandleader, Joe Stilgoe is a jazz musician with a magic touch, equally happy when topping the jazz charts or holding audiences spellbound with his very personal take on the Broadway classics. The Times raved over his ‘dazzling digits; but the man himself is disarmingly modest – “I suppose I’m only doing what my heroes did, like Cole Porter, Irving Berling and Frank Loesser”, he says. Expect an evening of just that, with his new all star trio, violinist/conductor Fiona Monbet and the BBC Concert Orchestra. The BBC Concert Orchestra collaborated on a live show for Joe’s smash 2022 album THEATRE; now, they reunite to play tracks from his latest album Welcome to the Club, including The Man In The Moon, Nobody and Mr Peanuts.

gig.title: Public Service Broadcasting
gig.pageText: Public Service Broadcasting return to Alexandra Palace on 26 September 2026 for their biggest ever headline show, celebrating 10 (+1) years of The Race For Space. Speaking about the Alexandra Palace show, Public Service Broadcasting’s J. Willgoose, Esq., said: “Being able to come back to Alexandra Palace – where we first launched the album in 2014 – and play our biggest ever headline show, in support of The Race For Space, is very special. That record means a great deal to us as a band, and we know it’s similarly important for a lot of our fans; we’re hoping to create a truly memorable, celebratory experience that will live long in the memory.” Public Service Broadcasting are a London-based band known for blending cinematic post-rock, electronics and archival audio to bring moments of history to life. Since their breakthrough album The Race For Space (2015), a gold-certified, chart-topping exploration of the space race, every studio album has reached the UK Top 5, including Every Valley, Bright Magic and 2024’s acclaimed The Last Flight. Celebrated for their immersive live performances, the band have built a reputation as one of the UK’s most ambitious and original live acts. Age restriction 16+

gig.title: Knit + Stitch
gig.pageText: Join us for Knit + Stitch, from 8 – 11 October 2026! Knit + Stitch returns to Alexandra Palace for 2026 – the biggest and best textile craft exhibition in the UK. Bringing together hundreds of crafting workshops, demonstrations, interactive features, curated Textile Art galleries, as well as over 300 of the leading specialist craft suppliers. Whether you’re shopping, learning, or just soaking in the atmosphere, Knit + Stitch is a must-visit for anyone with a crafty spark! Open to all ages. Under 5s do not require a ticket. Those aged 5 – 17 will need to purchase a child ticket.

gig.title: Mind Body Soul Experience
gig.pageText: The Mind Body Soul Experience is a celebration of everyone’s uniqueness, offering the tools you need to understand and achieve your potential. Get ready for a weekend of wellness, growth, and self-celebration. Take part in one of the many live classes run by renowned instructors and expert speakers including sound healing, animal spirit guides, chakra journeys, holistic energy, chakra dancing, finding your purpose, manifestation, lifestyle coaching and much more… Returning to the show this year are Meinl Sonic Energy, a leading innovator in sound healing instruments and meditative tools. They will be hosting live sound demonstrations, immersive mini sessions and offering expert guidance on meditation and therapeutic practices. Discover an array of holistic products and services in the marketplace including psychic and tarot readings, iridology readers, face readers, complementary therapies, energy therapy, mind coaching, chakra healing, as well as organic skincare, crystals and wellness retreats and many more. Whether you’re looking to connect with a higher power, with yourself, or just have fun – there’s something for everyone! Your entrance ticket Mind Body Soul Experience also includes entry to the OM Yoga Show and Vegan Life Live which takes place in the same venue over the weekend. Children under 16 can enter for free when accompanied with an adult. For more information, visit www.mindbodysoul.show

gig.title: OM Yoga Show
gig.pageText: The OM Yoga Show is one of Europe’s largest yoga events, offering the perfect introduction to the ancient practice of yoga. With over 200 live classes run by renowned instructors and expert speakers there is something for everyone, including Sound Healing, Traditional Yoga, Pilates, Hot Yoga, Cacao Ceremonies, Meditation, Face Yoga, Gong Baths and much, much more. New for 2026 is the FÔLD Reformer Pilates Area with FREE classes running over the weekend. Whether you’re a seasoned yogi or just starting your journey, this event is for everyone! Discover the latest yoga trends, shop for unique yoga gear, and connect with like-minded individuals. Don’t miss out on this amazing opportunity to find your inner peace and rejuvenate your mind, body, and soul. Your entrance ticket to the OM Yoga Show also includes entry to Mind Body Soul Experience and Vegan Life Live which take place in the same venue over the weekend. Children under 16 can enter for free when accompanied with an adult. For more information, visit omyogashow.com.

gig.title: Vegan Life Live
gig.pageText: Whether you are a long-time vegan or just curious about the lifestyle, Vegan Life Live is the ideal platform to learn, explore, and celebrate everything vegan. Vegan Life Live is the perfect place to connect with like-minded individuals. Engage in insightful conversations with experts, attend inspiring talks and gain valuable knowledge about living a compassionate and sustainable life. Guest speakers will lead FREE talks covering a wide range of topics ranging from activism, animal welfare, Q&A sessions, nutrition, fitness and much more. The food court is the perfect opportunity to sample a wide range of vegan cuisine including a diverse selection of hot and cold food, snacks, drinks and desserts from cultures around the world. We hope you’re hungry, because there’s so much to try! Shop till you drop at the vibrant marketplace showcasing everything vegan from the latest vegan products, skincare, clothing, supplements, gifts, ingredients and much more. Discover so many of the different ways that veganism is changing the world, and how it can benefit you! Your entrance ticket to Vegan Life Live also includes entry into OM Yoga Show and Mind Body Soul Experience which take place in the same venue over the weekend. Children under 16 can enter for free when accompanied with an adult. For more information, visit veganlifelive.com.

gig.title: Rhythm Stick Club Night – Live From Ally Pally
gig.pageText: Join us as our Victorian Theatre is transformed into Rhythm Stick – the most exclusive inclusive club night in London! Rhythm Stick is an inclusive club night designed by and for adults with disabilities, and it finally returns home to Alexandra Palace Theatre this October. Grab your glowsticks, slap on some glitter, don your best party fit and throw some shapes. Rhythm Stick is part of Live From Ally Pally, a programme of events that marks 90 years since the start of television broadcasting at Alexandra Palace. Essential companions go free, please add your free ticket during checkout. If you’d like to get involved with Rhythm Stick, we’re offering a free course to those who identify as disabled and want to learn about events management. Click the button below for more information,

gig.title: Beth Orton
gig.pageText: Folktronica pioneer Beth Orton brings her new album The Ground Above to Alexandra Palace Theatre this October. For more than three decades, Beth Orton has remained one of the most distinctive voices in contemporary music. Since her 1996 debut Trailer Park, she has built a catalogue marked by emotional clarity and constant evolution, from Comfort of Strangers to the spectral, self-produced Weather Alive. Released in 2022, Weather Alive became a major critical breakthrough, signaling not just a return but a reinvention. Her first self-produced album and debut for Partisan Records, it earned widespread acclaim, with The New York Times praising its “modal vocal phrases and marveling” storytelling, Pitchfork awarding Best New Music (8.7), and MOJO highlighting its richness and extraordinary writing. With The Ground Above, Orton returns with renewed urgency and conviction.

gig.title: Fat Freddy’s Drop
gig.pageText: Booty shaking soul monster Fat Freddy’s Drop returns to Alexandra Palace in 2026 to celebrate 21 years of Based on a True Story, their acclaimed debut album. Fat Freddy’s Drop are a seven-piece band from Wellington, Aotearoa, known for their fusion of dub, reggae, soul, funk and electronic influences. Their debut album Based On A True Story was released independently in 2005 and became Aotearoa’s longest-charting album, spending 111 weeks in the Top 40 and winning eight New Zealand Music Awards. The band’s 2026 tour marks their first shows since the passing of founding member Chris ‘MU’ Faiumu and continues their shared intention to celebrate the music they created together. Age restriction 16+ Plus very special guest DJ Nightmares On Wax

gig.title: The Reytons
gig.pageText: South Yorkshire’s Finest bring their World Tour to Alexandra Palace this October. Built on grit, working-class pride and sheer determination, The Reytons continue their ascent up the ladder of indie rock. Famous for their raucous live shows, and touted by many as the best live act of their generation, the British 4-piece pride themselves on their honesty and pure energy. Having taken their native UK by storm, with number one albums, sold out park shows and major festival headlines, the lads from Rotherham are taking on the world with their upcoming world tour.

gig.title: Crouch End Festival Chorus – Mozart Requiem
gig.pageText: Join us as we welcome back Crouch End Festival Chorus to Alexandra Palace Theatre this Autumn. Mozart’s cherished Requiem is intensely dramatic, with origins shrouded in mystery. Mozart received an anonymous commission for a Requiem Mass in 1791 and came to believe he was composing it for his own funeral. By the time of his death that December at the age of 35, it remained unfinished; it is widely believed that his pupil, Süssmayr, completed it but the space for doubt keeps alive the mystique. It is truly a masterpiece, with its extraordinary beauty, subtlety and profound expression touching each new generation. The first half of the concert includes works by Christopher Tin on the theme of flight including the iconic theme Sogno di Volare from the video game Civilization, to follow Gibbons’s pristine The Silver Swan, as well as Jessica Curry’s haunting Echo, a CEFC commission dedicated to her late father. Age recommendation: all ages welcome

gig.title: Overmono
gig.pageText: Overmono return to Alexandra Palace in October 2026 with their highly anticipated new album, Pure Devotion. Fresh from announcing their second album Pure Devotion (out 7 August via XL), the Russell brothers bring their most ambitious live show yet to Alexandra Palace. Tom and Ed Russell’s ever-evolving performance fuses emotional intensity with body-moving club energy, building on the global success of Good Lies. Expect a spellbinding night from one of the defining electronic acts of the decade. Age restriction 18+

gig.title: Gary Delaney – Gary On Laughing
gig.pageText: Gary Delaney’s last UK tour ran for two and a half years across 378 dates. People laughed a lot and kept coming back. His videos have hundreds of millions of views. So now he’s doing it all again, bringing his brand-new show to Alexandra Palace Theatre. All new jokes and utterly splendid filth. Come along. It’ll be fun. Don’t bring the kids or people who like to get their knickers in a twist. Do wear a TENA pad or dark trousers. Age recommendation: 16+

gig.title: London Bollywood Orchestra – Sounds Of Mumbai
gig.pageText: This Diwali, experience the spectacular sound of Bollywood live at Alexandra Palace Theatre as the London Bollywood Orchestra returns with its dazzling new concert, Sounds of Mumbai. Following sold-out performances across London, a successful UK tour and a hugely acclaimed debut at the Royal Festival Hall, the London Bollywood Orchestra brings audiences an unforgettable celebration of the greatest Bollywood songs ever written. From timeless classics of the 1940s and 50s to modern chart-topping favourites, Sounds of Mumbai is a vibrant musical journey through the soundtrack of generations. Led by acclaimed Music Director Tim Pottier, whose credits include the BBC Prom celebrating Lata Mangeshkar, the City of Birmingham Symphony Orchestra’s Best of Bollywood, and Sonu Nigam’s Rafi Resurrected, the orchestra features some of London’s finest musicians from the West End, leading orchestras and the jazz world. Age recommendation: 10+

gig.title: Skindred
gig.pageText: Skindred bring their signature mix of genres to Alexandra Palace this Halloween as part of the YOU GOT THIS Tour. Expect a high-energy night of metal, reggae and punk fusion, packed with massive riffs and feel-good anthems from the Nu-Metal titans. Skindred are a Welsh band known for pioneering ragga metal, blending heavy rock with reggae, dub and punk. Fronted by Benji Webbe, they’ve built a global following through chart success and explosive live performances, becoming one of the UK’s most distinctive and uplifting heavy acts. Plus Special Guests: Alien Ant Farm, Spineshank and Orgy Age restriction 16+

gig.title: Bill Ryder-Jones
gig.pageText: Experience Bill Ryder-Jones and the Royal Liverpool Philharmonic Orchestra performing If… and other works live at Alexandra Palace Theatre – marking 15 years of his acclaimed debut with a rare full-album orchestral performance, plus new material and expanded favourites. Bill Ryder-Jones is a Wirral-born composer, producer and former guitarist of The Coral. Renowned for his emotive solo work, he blends orchestral arrangements with indie songwriting, earning critical acclaim for albums including If…, West Kirby County Primary and Iechyd Da. Age restriction 16+

gig.title: Courteeners
gig.pageText: God Bless The Band! Courteeners bring their huge 20th‑anniversary tour to Alexandra Palace this autumn. Celebrating two decades of era‑defining indie, Courteeners head to Ally Pally as part of their nationwide tour marking the release of God Bless The Band and new single The Luckiest Man Alive. The new best‑of album lands 28 August 2026, spanning highlights from all seven studio albums plus two brand‑new tracks. Since their 2008 debut St. Jude, Courteeners have become one of Britain’s biggest live acts. Led by Liam Fray, the band’s anthemic songwriting and communal live shows have earned them over a million UK album sales, multiple Top 5 records and a devoted following. Twenty years on, Courteeners remain a defining force in modern indie music. Age restriction 16+

gig.title: Enter Shikari
gig.pageText: Enter Shikari return to Alexandra Palace in 2026 for a huge headline show. Since forming in St Albans in 2003, Enter Shikari have become one of the most forward-thinking and influential bands in British alternative music. Blending post-hardcore, electronica and punk with fearless ambition, they’ve released seven acclaimed studio albums, all debuting in the UK Top 5, with 2023’s A Kiss For The Whole World earning their first Official UK Album Chart #1. Famed for their electrifying live shows, the band have played around 3,000 concerts worldwide (including a few here!), headlined arenas and major festivals, and won multiple Best Live Band awards from Kerrang!, NME, Rock Sound and the Heavy Music Awards. With new music underway and 2026 just beginning, Enter Shikari return to Ally Pally ready to ignite the next chapter. Age restriction 16+

gig.title: Sherlock Holmes and the 12 Days of Christmas
gig.pageText: It’s Christmas in Victorian London. In the West End, performers are suddenly dropping dead mid-scene. When the world’s greatest detective, Sherlock Holmes, uncovers a chilling connection to The Twelve Days of Christmas, he knows something sinister is afoot. With the body count rising and time running out, Sherlock must catch the killer before the next murder. But as he hurtles towards a deadly showdown, will this be the case that finally brings down the great detective? Perfectly set at Alexandra Palace Theatre, one of London’s most atmospheric Victorian theatres, audiences can immerse themselves in a festive murder mystery packed with mayhem, mischief and Christmas cheer!

gig.title: Blossoms
gig.pageText: Blossoms bring their biggest tour yet and new album Songs From The Wedding Cake to the Palace this November. Age restriction 16+

gig.title: Gorgon City
gig.pageText: For the first time since 2019, Gorgon City return with a brand-new live show, this time taking over the Great Hall at Alexandra Palace for a very special headline performance this November. Following a run of global successes, the duo step back on stage with an immersive new production, blending their biggest tracks with deeper cuts and unreleased material. Known for their signature mix of tech house energy and melodic hooks, Gorgon City’s live shows deliver a powerful, fully realised experience. Age restriction 18+

gig.title: Cinderella On Ice
gig.pageText: This festive season, step into a world of enchantment as Cinderella on Ice glides into Alexandra Palace. Against the sparkling backdrop of our historic ice rink, this beloved fairy tale is brought to life through elegant skating, dazzling costumes and magical storytelling. From a fairy godmother’s spell to the grand royal ball, follow Cinderella’s unforgettable journey in a spectacular production filled with wonder, charm and festive cheer. Performed by our talented community of amateur skaters, who train throughout the year to create this much-loved seasonal tradition, Cinderella on Ice is a celebration of creativity, dedication and the joy of live performance. Presented by Alexandra Palace Ice Rink Amateur Productions

gig.title: Paddy Power World Darts Championship 2026/2027
gig.pageText: The Paddy Power World Darts Championship returns to Alexandra Palace from 11 December 2026 to 3 January 2027, with Sport’s Biggest Party moving into the Great Hall for the first time. With a record 180,000 tickets available, the tournament will be bigger than ever. For the first time, tickets will be allocated via a ballot system. There are two opportunities to apply: PDCTV Annual Members Ballot: Priority access for PDCTV Annual Members, offering an increased opportunity to secure tickets PDCTV Annual Membership deadline: 23:59 BST, Sunday 30 August 2026 Ballot opens: 12:00 BST, Tuesday 1 September 2026 Ballot closes: 23:59 BST, Monday 7 September 2026 Become a member General Ballot: Open to all fans Ballot opens: 12:00 BST, Tuesday 8 September 2026 Ballot closes: 23:59 BST, Monday 14 September 2026 Register your interest

gig.title: Johnstone’s Paint Masters Snooker 2027
gig.pageText: The Johnstone’s Paint Masters Snooker 2027 will once again take place at Alexandra Palace in January 2027. Steeped in history and prestige, the Masters is snooker’s greatest invitation event and a cornerstone of the sport’s iconic Triple Crown, alongside the World Championship and the UK Championship. First staged in 1975, it remains one of the most coveted titles in snooker, reserved exclusively for the world’s top 16 ranked players, making every match an elite contest of skill and strategy. Held at Alexandra Palace since 2012, the tournament is renowned for its electric atmosphere, with over 2,000 passionate fans creating an unforgettable setting for world-class snooker. The event is televised on BBC Sport, Eurosport, TNT, CCTV5, and international partners, allowing millions around the globe to experience the drama, skill, and tradition of the Masters. Age restriction: All ages welcome, under 16s must be accompanied by an adult over 21

gig.title: What’s Love Got To Do With It
gig.pageText: After a fantastic sell-out debut tour across the UK, Tina Turner fans will have the time of their lives as What’s Love Got To Do With It? returns to Alexandra Palace Theatre in 2027, celebrating the music and career of this incredible rock and soul legend. Expect a night of high energy and feel-good rock- and-roll, performed by an all-live band. This joyous show features all the hits including Proud Mary, River Deep, Simply The Best, Private Dancer, and many more! Please note that this is a tribute production and is not endorsed by or affiliated with the Tina Turner Estate. Age recommendation: 16+

gig.title: Jordan Rakei
gig.pageText: Jordan Rakei brings his biggest-ever headline show to Alexandra Palace as part of the A Safe Place To Be Wild Tour in April 2027. Following the announcement of his new album A Safe Place To Be Wild, the Grammy-winning singer, songwriter, producer and multi-instrumentalist returns to London for the biggest headline show of his career. Expect music from the forthcoming record, including latest single Enemies, alongside fan favourites from across his celebrated catalogue, which blends soul, jazz and R&B into a distinctive sound. Across six acclaimed albums, collaborations with Bonobo, Tom Misch and Loyle Carner, and sold-out shows at the Royal Albert Hall, he has established himself as one of the UK’s most compelling live performers. Age restriction 16+

gig.title: Weezer
gig.pageText: Weezer bring The Gathering World Tour to Alexandra Palace in May 2027. Venue pre-sale Thursday 13 August, 10am – set a reminder on DICE for access General sale Friday 14 August, 10am Fresh from announcing their new self-titled album Weezer, the legendary alt-rock band return to London as part of a major international tour celebrating their 20th studio album. Fans can expect new music including recent singles Shine Again, We Might as Well Be Strangers (feat. Wednesday) and C.E.O., alongside the band’s catalogue of era-defining hits. Across more than three decades, Weezer have become one of the most influential and enduring rock bands of their generation, with thousands of shows, countless anthems and a legacy that continues to inspire new generations of musicians. Special guests Taking Back Sunday will support. Age restriction 16+

gig.title: Dylan Moran – Looking For Trouble
gig.pageText: Showtime. What are you going to do? Are you going to go to work? Or stay in bed, chasing oblivion. Guess what? We’re fresh out of oblivion. The Economy will do fine without you – but how long will you survive without the usual giant horn of frozen caramel latte and the five thousand other pieces of bullshit you have smushed together so you can point at it and croak ‘That’s my ..life?’ Now, now, all this drama and we’re not even out the door yet. Find out how it could all have been different. Find out how to reclaim your life by becoming a lethal kickboxing, chess champion. Pioneer new trends in global lovemaking, join tan elite band trillionaire poet/pastry chef/mountineers. Just go BAFTA and Perrier Award-winning comedian and star of Black Books, Dylan Moran, brings his brand new show to Alexandra Palace Theatre in May 2027 for two nights only. Age recommendation: 16+

gig.title: Ed Byrne – No Dramas
gig.pageText: Ed Byrne makes his debut at Alexandra Palace Theatre for one night only in July 2027, with his brand new stand-up show No Dramas. Ed just wants to live a life free of hassles or drama. He feels he’s earned it, but the world has other plans for him. Come, hear the conquistador of petty gripes air his grievances with a world hell-bent on irritating the bejeezus out of us all and, who knows, perhaps it will make you feel better about your own bouts of impotent rage. Age recommendation: 16+

gig.title: Kaleidoscope Festival
gig.pageText: Kaleidoscope Festival returns to Alexandra Palace Park following a sell-out year, bringing together live music, comedy, culture and family entertainment in one unforgettable setting. Tier 1 tickets are now on sale at the best available price, with flexible payment plans available to help spread the cost. Line-up announcements coming later this year! All ages welcome Under 16s to be accompanied by an adult over the age of 21
